title: New material added via data.materials.append() renders unused because faces still point at the old slot index
problem: Calling obj.data.materials.append(new_mat) adds a new slot but does NOT reassign any polygon's material_index to point at it. If slot 0 already existed (e.g. empty/null from object creation) and the new material became slot 1, every face keeps material_index=0, so the newly 'assigned' material renders on zero faces even though it appears in the material list.
symptom: obj.data.materials shows the expected material name(s), but sorted(set(p.material_index for p in obj.data.polygons)) == [0] where slot 0 is null or a different material -- the intended material is present but structurally orphaned.

fix.summary: After appending a material, explicitly set polygon.material_index to the new slot's index for the faces that should use it (usually all faces for a single-material object), then remove any now-empty slots.
bpy_bmesh_steps: for p in obj.data.polygons: p.material_index = target_slot_index
fix.code_snippet: verified directly against Bottle and Flashlight in runs/2026-08-07_decision-cycles/ (decisions 040-042)

evidence.note: bpy.ops.object.material_slot_remove_unused() reported 'Removed 1 slots' without fixing the actual defect -- verify with a direct polygon.material_index scan, don't trust the operator's own report

applicability: Any time a material is programmatically assigned via data.materials.append() (or a material appears unassigned/unused after seeming to be set), check polygon.material_index distribution before trusting that shading is correct.

runtime_usage.problem: Accent material existed in slot 1 but no polygon used it
runtime_usage.action: Assign the intended top-half polygons to material slot 1
